title: New York defies Trump admin, asks court to shut down Polymarket gambling
gist: New York sued Polymarket US (QCX LLC) as an unlicensed gambling operation, seeking a shutdown order, fines, disgorgement and restitution, mirroring its July suit against Kalshi, while the CFTC under the Trump administration asserts exclusive federal jurisdiction. A Third Circuit vs. Ninth Circuit split on whether sports event contracts are federally regulated 'swaps' makes a Supreme Court ruling the likely decider for the whole prediction-market sports-betting model.

insights.claim: New York State sued Polymarket's US entity (QCX LLC, a.k.a. Polymarket US) in New York County court, seeking an order stopping it from operating as an unlicensed gambling business plus fines, forfeiture of all illegal gains, and restitution to users.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Disgorgement and restitution demands create direct financial liability for Polymarket US, not just an operating restriction; watch for injunction rulings.
insights.quote: seeking a court order stopping Polymarket from operating as an unlicensed gambling business and requiring the company to pay fines, forfeit all illegal gains and pay restitution to users.
insights.locator: The New York press release said

insights.claim: New York argues prediction-market sports contracts evade the gambling taxes paid by licensed casinos and mobile sportsbooks, revenue the state uses to fund schools, youth sports and problem-gambling treatment.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: State tax revenue at stake gives states a strong fiscal motive to keep fighting prediction markets regardless of federal posture; tax-arbitrage advantage vs. licensed sportsbooks is the core regulatory risk.
insights.quote: sidestepping its obligation to pay taxes like licensed casinos and mobile sports gambling platforms do

insights.claim: Polymarket's US product is available to 18–20 year olds, while New York law requires bettors to be at least 21 for mobile sports betting, a consumer-protection angle the state is emphasizing.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Underage-access allegations are politically potent and could drive age-gating requirements that shrink prediction markets' addressable user base.
insights.locator: Polymarket is “available to users between the ages of 18–20

insights.claim: New York's complaint cites specific Polymarket sports markets, including a Packers vs. Giants NFL game, the February 2026 Super Bowl winner, and a March 20, 2026 Hofstra vs. Alabama college basketball game, as bets meeting the state-law definition of gambling.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Sports contracts, likely a major volume driver, are the specific target; non-sports event markets are less exposed under this theory.
insights.locator: The lawsuit said examples of bets

insights.claim: The Trump administration's CFTC sides with prediction markets and asserts exclusive federal jurisdiction over them, going so far as to declare a 'market emergency' in New York in August to block the state from applying gambling laws to Kalshi.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Federal regulatory backing is the prediction markets' main shield; a change in CFTC leadership or posture would materially raise their risk.

insights.claim: Federal appeals courts are split: the Third Circuit ruled New Jersey cannot regulate sports bets on prediction markets, while the Ninth Circuit ruled Nevada can stop Kalshi from offering sports bets, hinging on whether such contracts are federally defined 'swaps' regulated only by the CFTC.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: The 'swap' definition question is the single legal variable that determines whether the national prediction-market sports model survives; track it as a binary catalyst.
insights.locator: The Supreme Court may ultimately decide

insights.claim: The Supreme Court is likely to ultimately decide whether states can restrict or prohibit sports betting on prediction markets, and New Jersey has already urged the Court to take up the question.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: A cert grant would set a clear timeline for a nationwide resolution affecting Kalshi, Polymarket and incumbent sportsbooks alike.
insights.quote: Companies like Kalshi claim to offer legal sports betting in all 50 states, but they refuse to follow the gambling laws of any state

insights.claim: State enforcement against prediction markets is broadening: beyond New York's suits against Kalshi (July) and Polymarket, Kentucky sued Polymarket in June, and Kalshi has sued other states after receiving cease-and-desist orders.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Multi-state litigation raises legal costs and fragmentation risk for prediction markets and signals coordinated state resistance.
insights.locator: While Kentucky sued Polymarket in June

insights.claim: Polymarket's main platform has been unavailable in the US since 2022, when the CFTC ruled it an illegally unregistered exchange; its site is view-only in the US though users can bypass the restriction with a VPN.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: VPN leakage to the offshore exchange is an ongoing compliance exposure for Polymarket.
insights.locator: Polymarket’s main platform technically hasn’t been available

insights.claim: Polymarket entered the US via a limited mobile app in December 2025 after acquiring CFTC-licensed firm QCX, and is still seeking CFTC permission to bring its main exchange back to the US.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Buying a licensed entity was Polymarket's regulatory shortcut; the CFTC decision on the main exchange is a key upside catalyst while state suits are the downside.
insights.locator: Polymarket is seeking the CFTC’s permission

insights.claim: The Wall Street Journal reported in June that Polymarket promoted itself in the US by paying dozens of social media users to film themselves making fake bets on copies of the Polymarket website.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Aggressive marketing practices add reputational and consumer-protection ammunition for state regulators.
insights.locator: Polymarket promoted its platform in the US

insights.claim: Polymarket dismissed New York's suit as a 'copy/paste' of the Kalshi case, said it has over 350 employees in New York and will stay, and signaled it will fight in court rather than exit the state.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Polymarket is choosing litigation over withdrawal, so the outcome will likely track the broader Kalshi/Supreme Court resolution.
insights.quote: While the AG’s decision to copy/paste a recycled lawsuit is disappointing, we’ll fight for our users.
